title: Third mode denied — Eugubinus and Vorstius confine substance to heaven
source_text: XII. Sed de tertio modo, nimirum de praesentia secundum substantiam, repertus est unus, aut alter qui negaret Deum ita ubique esse. Nam inter Pontificios Augustinus quidam Eugubinus scribens in Psalmum 138. juxta versionem vulgatam, qui juxta Hebraeos est 139. pretendit Deum secundum substantiam extra caelum non esse, & in caelo duntaxat versari. Ex reformatis vero similem errorem erravit Vorstius, sub hujus saeculi initium, Professor in Academia Lugduno-Batava, qui affirmavit Deum, ratione suae substantiae, esse tantum in caelo, licet in terra virtute & sapientia sua nobis adsit.
pass_a_gloss: But concerning the third mode, namely presence according to substance, one or another has been found who would deny that God is thus everywhere. For among the Pontificals a certain Augustinus Eugubinus writing on Psalm 138 according to the Vulgate version, which according to the Hebrews is 139, maintains that God according to substance is not outside heaven, and dwells only in heaven. But from the Reformed Vorstius erred with a like error at the beginning of this century, Professor in the Academy of Leiden, who affirmed that God, by reason of His substance, is only in heaven, although on earth He is present to us by His power and wisdom.
pass_b_english: Eugubinus: God's substance only in heaven (Ps 138/139).
Vorstius (Leiden): same — substance in heaven; earth only by power/wisdom.
